Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
The divisors of \(250=2\cdot 5^3\) are

\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250,
\]

which can be written as \(5^b\) and \(2\cdot 5^b\) for \(b=0,1,2,3\).

First, from the condition,

\[
|A_i|=|A_i\cap A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i.
\]

If \(m\mid n\), then

\[
|A_m\cap A_n|=\gcd(m,n)=m=|A_m|,
\]

so \(A_m\subseteq A_n\). Also, if \(g=\gcd(i,j)\), then \(A_g\subseteq A_i\cap A_j\) and both sets have size \(g\), so

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_g.
\]

---

### Lower bound

Let

\[
O_b=A_{5^b},\qquad E_b=A_{2\cdot 5^b}\qquad (b=0,1,2,3).
\]

Then

\[
|O_b|=5^b,\qquad |E_b|=2\cdot 5^b,
\]

and \(O_b\subseteq E_b\). Also, if \(a\ge b\), then

\[
O_a\cap E_b=A_{5^b}=O_b,
\]

so

\[
|O_a\cup E_b|=5^a+2\cdot 5^b-5^b=5^a+5^b.
\]

Suppose some of these eight sets are contained in \(\{1,2,\dots,t\}\). Let \(a\) be the largest index with \(O_a\subseteq [t]\), and \(b\) the largest index with \(E_b\subseteq [t]\). Since \(O_b\subseteq E_b\), we have \(b\le a\).

The possible values of \((a,b)\), the number of contained sets, and the size of \(O_a\cup E_b\) are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
(a,b) & \#\text{ sets} & 5^a+5^b\\
\hline
(0,-1)&1&1\\
(0,0)&2&2\\
(1,-1)&2&5\\
(1,0)&3&6\\
(1,1)&4&10\\
(2,-1)&3&25\\
(2,0)&4&26\\
(2,1)&5&30\\
(2,2)&6&50\\
(3,-1)&4&125\\
(3,0)&5&126\\
(3,1)&6&130\\
(3,2)&7&150\\
(3,3)&8&250
\end{array}
\]

Thus, to have at least \(k\) of the eight sets with maximum \(\le t\), we must have

\[
t\ge r_k,
\]

where

\[
(r_1,\dots,r_8)=(1,2,6,10,30,50,150,250).
\]

Let \(M_1\le M_2\le \cdots\le M_8\) be the eight maxima \(\max A_d\). Then \(M_k\ge r_k\) for each \(k\). Hence

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
\ge 1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250
=499.
\]

---

### Construction attaining the bound

For each positive integer \(d\), choose a set \(B_d\) with \(|B_d|=\varphi(d)\), all the \(B_d\) disjoint. For the divisors of \(250\), choose

\[
\begin{aligned}
B_1&=\{1\},\\
B_2&=\{2\},\\
B_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
B_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
B_{25}&=\{11,12,\dots,30\},\\
B_{50}&=\{31,32,\dots,50\},\\
B_{125}&=\{51,52,\dots,150\},\\
B_{250}&=\{151,152,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For all other \(d\), choose disjoint sets \(B_d\) of size \(\varphi(d)\) using integers greater than \(250\).

Now define

\[
A_n=\bigcup_{d\mid n} B_d.
\]

Since the \(B_d\) are disjoint,

\[
A_i\cap A_j=\bigcup_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)} B_d=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

Therefore

\[
|A_i\cap A_j|
=|A_{\gcd(i,j)}|
=\sum_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(d)
=\gcd(i,j).
\]

So this construction satisfies the required condition.

The maxima are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\
\hline
\max A_d&1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]

and their sum is

\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}.
\]
